outcome.technical: tools/sweep-selftests.py: file_timeout gains staged= and cap=; a staged suite with no entry gets the largest calibrated timeout any table entry (ghosts included) would get at the same slots, an ordinary untimed file the floor, every answer bounded by cap. New on_ci()/sweep_deadline(): on CI (CI=true) sweep(deadline=SWEEP_DEADLINE) cuts each file's timeout to what is left of the deadline when it is admitted, so a hang is named before the job limit; default_jobs reuses on_ci. SWEEP_DEADLINE=1380, CI_SETUP_ALLOWANCE=120, arithmetic in the comment: 26 min = 1560s, minus 120s setup (observed 12-18s before and under 5s after the sweep step in both Windows runs), minus 60s render margin. TIMEOUT_PER_COST 8 -> 3: the table is now Windows seconds, and across the two runs' Windows plain+cp1252 cells no file of 20s or more varied by more than 1.51x. costs_from_render keeps a file's LONGEST timing when a log holds it twice. budget_line prints the deadline when one applies. Comments and the table's about text now say the table decides balance AND timeouts, and that a stale table can cost balance and a too-tight timeout for a file that grew, never coverage, and that omission tightens nothing. .github/sweep-costs.json re-recorded from the 12 Windows plain/cp1252 cell logs of runs 38379717433 and 38382182020 concatenated, via --costs-from-log --platform windows-latest --workers 4 (all 331 swept files timed; test_drive_phase now 1346.4 slot-seconds, so its calibrated timeout is 1347s). .github/workflows/ci.yml: selftests timeout-minutes 25 -> 26, which is only what the deadline needs to sit above 1347s; the header rule now says two to three times the longest run, with a five-minute floor for a job whose three times is under five minutes (lint, plugin-validate), and notes run 38382182020 found no job longer than the recorded figures; the WHY THREE PARTS block uses the Windows table, the measured 380-540s sweep steps, the deadline, and the new record recipe. tools/gate-parity.py: job_bound_evidence also reports a bound over max(3x longest, 5 min) (BOUND_CEILING_FACTOR, BOUND_FLOOR_MINUTES); new case jb4 (red first: 131/132 before the implementation), jb1/jb2 fixtures adjusted, summary line updated. CONTRIBUTING.md sweep block says what the table decides, what staleness costs, and the CI deadline. plugins/audit/tests/_harness.py unchanged: `grep -n -i 'two.core\|2.core'` exits 1, so no two-core wording is left there; P127.1's title rename is the orchestrator's. docs/audit/phases/P127.json not touched by me. Runs: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py` exit 0, 331/331 files ok, 15840 cases (sweep-selftests 94 cases, gate-parity 132, prove-gates 37). Also run as dev checks, not reported as gates: `ruff check plugins/audit tools` exit 0; `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` exit 0. The full mutating `tools/prove-gates.py` run was not done because it mutates the shared tree; `--list` shows no row for job_bound_evidence or the sweep timeout functions.
outcome.descriptive: A cost table missing a file can no longer tighten its timeout, the timeouts come from Windows timings, and on CI the sweep names a hung file before the job's own time limit cancels it.
